column7:
Penyedia Jasa Pembayaran (PJP) [Payment Service Provider] — Activity Bundle Licence

PBI 10/2025 replaces the previous Category 1/2/3 model with an activity-bundling approach. Licences are granted based on the specific bundle of activities to be performed:

a. Bundle 1A — Source of Funds Administration (deposits, e-money value, deferred payment/BNPL) + full payment transaction forwarding (data forwarding + digital/non-digital fund transfer). Available to Primary PSPs (PSP Utama) only.

b. Bundle 1B — Same scope as Bundle 1A with certain restrictions on source-of-funds and/or fund transfer sub-activities. Available to both Primary and Non-Primary PSPs.

c. Bundle 2 — Payment transaction forwarding only (acquiring/payment gateway, fund transfer digital and non-digital). No source-of-funds administration. Available to Primary and Non-Primary PSPs.

d. Bundle 3 — Non-digital fund transfer / remittance services only. Available to Non-Primary PSPs; excluded for Commercial Banks and Rural Banks (BPR).

Penyelenggara Infrastruktur Sistem Pembayaran (PIP) [Payment Infrastructure Provider]
— Designation (Penetapan) by Bank Indonesia, not a standard licence. Activities: clearing and settlement (including principal, switching, clearing, and dispute-resolution services for PIP members). PIP must be a non-bank entity (LSB) incorporated as a limited liability company.

PGSP:
License as a Payment Service Provider (PJP) is required for any entity acting as a PJP that facilitates payment transactions for end-users.Entities: Commercial Banks (Bank Umum) and Non-Bank Entities (Lembaga Selain Bank Umum / LSBU). Activity Bundling: The license is granted alongside specific "Activity Bundles 1, 2, and  3". 
These bundles dictate the exact scope of services the entity is legally permitted to including (i) Funds Management (management of payment accounts and the issuance of and/or provision of access to Funds) and (ii) the processing of payment transactions (the processing of payment transaction data and the processing of payment instructions, which may be accompanied by the facilitation of the receipt of payment proceeds through the provision of sub-accounts to Goods and/or Services Providers; and the processing of fund transfer instructions, both digital and non-digital).

Designation as a Payment System Infrastructure Provider (PIP), Bank Indonesia issues a formal designation for entities operating the core infrastructure that facilitates fund transfers between participants. Entities: Non-Bank Entities formulated as Limited Liability Companies (Perseroan Terbatas). This designation is specifically granted for clearing and/or final settlement (setelmen) activities.
column10:
Initial Capital Requirements (Minimum Paid-Up Capital):

PJP — by activity bundle (exact amounts specified in PADG 32/2025; relative hierarchy):
• Bundle 1A (Primary PSPs only): Highest tier
• Bundle 1B: Lower than Bundle 1A
• Bundle 2: Lower than Bundle 1B
• Bundle 3: Lowest tier

Note: Legacy amounts under PBI 23/6/2021 (Cat. 1: IDR 15 billion; Cat. 2: IDR 5 billion; Cat. 3: IDR 500 million / IDR 1 billion) remain reference points pending full PADG 32/2025 publication.

PIP: IDR 100 billion minimum paid-up capital.
Foreign principals: grandfathering provisions with letter of guarantee to BI.

Ongoing Capital (new requirement under PBI 10/2025):
• Minimum 10% of risk-weighted transactions, plus
• Surcharge of 1.5%–2.5% of risk-weighted transactions (PJP), or
• Surcharge of 2.5%–5.0% of risk-weighted transactions (PIP)

Transition: PJPs/PIPs that do not yet meet new requirements have 3 years from 31 March 2026 to comply (extendable by 2 years with BI approval).
